correct_answer: March 14 — use the latest academically-related activity across all courses in the payment period (ENG 204 and SOC 150 submissions on 3/14), provided those submissions constitute academically-related activity.
rationale: Federal R2T4 regulations require using the later of the student's last date of attendance or last date of academically-related activity. For a student enrolled in multiple courses, you use the latest activity across ALL courses in the payment period — not the earliest. The Canvas data shows submissions (not just logins) in ENG 204 on March 14, with 4 of 4 assignments submitted, which constitutes academically-related activity (submissions are explicitly qualifying under ED guidance). The MATH 210 situation (instructor absence, Feb 28 last activity) is relevant for other purposes but does NOT override the later activity in other courses. Kenji's guidance in Slack is correct on this point. Answer A incorrectly uses the earliest date and conflates per-course analysis with the R2T4 payment period calculation. Answer B arrives at the right date but for the wrong reason — the withdrawal form date is not automatically the LDA for R2T4; you must independently verify academic activity. Answer D raises a valid question about whether discussion posts qualify, but the Canvas log shows 'submissions' (4 of 4 due) not merely logins, and the unresolved Slack thread questioning this is a red herring — submissions are academically related activity per regulation. The instructor absence email, while contextually important, does not change the calculation since the student had activity in other courses through March 14.
